factProposals.value: A periodontal chart is one examination of one patient at one moment, holding up to 192 site readings: six sites per permanent tooth (distal, middle and mesial on the cheek side and on the tongue side), each with a probing depth and a recession in whole millimetres from 0 to 15 and a yes/no bleeding-on-probing answer. The tooth is stored as its FDI key; attachment loss is probing depth plus recession and is computed on read, never stored.

Anyone who may read clinical documentation (dentist, hygienist, assistant, admin) can see a patient's periodontal charts; only roles that manage clinical notes (dentist, hygienist, admin) can save one. The assistant reads but is refused (403) on save and is shown no save button; front desk and billing cannot see the tab and are refused (403) by the API; anonymous callers get 401.

The Periodontal tab of the patient workspace lists a patient's charts newest first (who took each, when, the number of sites and teeth, the share of sites that bled, the number of sites 4 mm or deeper, the deepest site) with a table of every reading including derived attachment loss. No chart on record is stated as 'none has been taken, not that the gums are healthy', and a failed load is stated as a failed load.

Incorrect charting data is refused with every problem listed together (tooth, site, field, a stable code and a message naming the allowed range), and nothing partial is saved: a depth or recession outside 0 to 15 mm or not a whole number, an unknown tooth, a primary tooth, an unknown site, a site entered twice, a value left out (never defaulted to 0 or 'no'), an empty chart. The screen checks the same rules first, marks each box and links the problem list to the boxes; the database refuses the same data again.

Every saved chart is written to the audit log with the signed-in user and a timestamp in the same save as the chart and its readings, so a chart cannot exist without its log entry and a failed log write stores nothing; the audit text carries no tooth or measurement. A failed save is reported as 'nothing was recorded' without database detail.

A saved periodontal chart and its readings can never be edited or deleted (database triggers 51064 and 51065); a correction is a new chart. The database also holds the tooth, site and millimetre ranges as case-sensitive check constraints and one reading per tooth and site per chart.

decisions.statement: A saved chart is immutable, and a correction is recorded as a new chart (the screen offers 'start a new chart from these values').
decisions.rationale: A periodontal chart is a clinical record of what was found at a moment; editing it would erase that, and the trust criterion requires every charting entry to be logged. A new chart keeps every earlier finding in the history.

decisions.statement: A save carries a client-chosen idempotency key, unique per patient: the same key with the same readings returns the chart already saved, and the same key with different readings is refused with 409 rather than ignored.
decisions.rationale: A dropped connection or double click must not create a second chart or a second audit entry, but silently dropping a different set of readings would lose clinical data without anyone knowing.

decisions.statement: Charting covers permanent teeth only, and recession cannot be negative.
decisions.rationale: The story names probing depth, recession and bleeding without dentition detail; primary teeth are not routinely probed and gingival overgrowth needs a different measure. Both are narrow to widen later (the key list and one database check).

decisions.statement: A reading needs both a probing depth and a recession (0 if there is none), and bleeding is a yes/no checkbox where unchecked means no.
decisions.rationale: A blank must never be read as 0 mm, so the person has to type 0; bleeding alone is not a measurement, so a site with only the box ticked is reported as incomplete.

decisions.statement: Reading charts needs ViewClinicalDocumentation and saving one needs ManageClinicalNotes, the same permissions as the odontogram and clinical notes.
decisions.rationale: Periodontal charting is clinical documentation, and reusing the existing permissions keeps the role matrix unchanged (no new permission was introduced).

limitations.statement: A chart is not linked to an encounter, diagnosis or treatment plan; it belongs to the patient and the moment. Linking is left for the structured diagnosis story.
Charting does not read the odontogram, so a tooth recorded there as missing can still be charted; a clinician leaves it empty.
No mobility, furcation, plaque or suppuration measures, no automatic periodontal staging or grading, and no printed or exported chart.
There is no draft saved on the server: entries not yet saved are lost if the page is closed, and the screen lists only the latest 20 charts.
Messages from the server name teeth by FDI number whatever numbering system the grid shows (the screen says so when it shows them).
